w: I apologize you for the delay.
r: I apologize to you for the delay.
y: Apologize to a person, for a reason.
a: Most people just say: sorry for the delay!
e: He apologized to his boss.
We apologize for the noise.
q: Apologize needs to before the person.
s: Save this for your next work email.

w: I'm so exciting about the trip!
r: I'm so excited about the trip!
y: -ed is how you feel. -ing is the thing.
a: I'm exciting means people get excited by you!
e: The game was exciting.
The kids are excited.
q: The movie causes the feeling, so -ing.
s: Send this to an excited friend.

w: The tickets are finished.
r: The tickets are sold out.
y: Sold out means none are left to buy.
a: A sold-out show is a big success!
e: The concert is sold out.
Sorry, that size is sold out.
q: We can't go. The show is ___.
Sold out means no tickets left.
s: Save this before you buy tickets.

w: Let's hang the picture on the floor.
r: Let's hang the picture on the wall.
y: Hang means put something up on a wall or hook.
a: Hang out means spend time!
e: Hang your coat here.
She hung a photo above the bed.
m: HANG = up on a wall or hook
q: Can you help me ___ this painting?
We hang pictures on a wall.
s: Save this and share it with a friend.

w: re-CON-ci-li-a-tion
r: re-con-ci-li-A-tion
y: Before -tion, the stress jumps to A.
a: The verb is different: RE-con-cile!
e: The bank reconciliation is done.
There was a reconciliation between them.
q: Where is the stress in reconciliation?
s: Save this for your next meeting.

w: I can't cope stress.
r: I can't cope with stress.
y: Cope needs with before the problem.
a: Deal with works the same way!
e: How do you cope with pressure?
She coped well with the change.
s: Send this to a stressed friend.

w: Doctors urge that people to rest.
r: Doctors urge people to rest.
y: Urge someone to do something.
a: Urge is stronger than ask!
e: They urged us to leave.
I urge you to read it.
q: Urge is followed by a person and to plus verb.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: She is credited for the idea.
r: She is credited with the idea.
y: Be credited with means people say you did it.
a: News writers use this a lot!
e: He will be credited with saving the team.
She was credited with the discovery.
q: Edison is credited ___ the light bulb.
The phrase is be credited with.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: We rely in technology.
r: We rely on technology.
y: Rely always takes on.
a: Depend works the same: depend on!
e: You can rely on me.
Many people rely on their phones.
s: Save this. You can rely on it!

w: The storm harmed the roof.
r: The storm damaged the roof.
y: Things get damaged. People get harmed.
a: Too much sun can harm your skin!
e: The car was damaged.
Smoking harms your health.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: Don't go at the full hours.
r: Don't go at peak times.
y: Peak times are when the most people come.
a: Off-peak times are cheaper!
e: Trains are crowded at peak times.
Prices are higher at peak times.
q: The gym is very busy at ___ times.
s: Save this and avoid the crowds.

w: There were approximately 52 people exactly.
r: There were approximately 50 people.
y: Approximately means about, not exactly.
a: In speech, people say about or around!
e: It takes approximately two hours.
Approximately half of us agreed.
s: Save this for your next report.

w: GEE-pee-ay
r: gee-pee-AY
y: In letter words, stress the last letter.
a: Same with USA and FBI!
e: My GPA is 3.5.
You need a good GPA.
q: Where is the stress in GPA?
s: Save this before your interview.

w: There's a risk to get sick.
r: There's a risk of getting sick.
y: Risk of plus -ing or noun.
a: But: risk losing money, as a verb, has no of!
e: There is a risk of fire.
Smoking raises the risk of cancer.
q: There's a high risk ___ rain today.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: I keep putting off to call him.
r: I keep putting off calling him.
y: Put off plus -ing means delay doing it.
a: Put off can also mean make you dislike something!
e: Stop putting off your homework.
We put off buying a car.
s: Save this. Don't put it off!

w: Nobody told me, but I did it.
r: I took the initiative to fix it.
y: Took the initiative shows you acted on your own.
a: Interviewers love hearing this phrase!
e: I took the initiative to train new staff.
She took the initiative to call the client.
m: no one asked → TOOK THE INITIATIVE
q: I took the ___ to plan the event.
The phrase is take the initiative.
s: Save this for your next interview.

w: The number of student are increasing.
r: The number of students is increasing.
y: The number takes is. A number takes are.
a: A number of students are here. Both rules work!
e: The number of cars is growing.
A number of people are waiting.
m: THE number IS, A number ARE
q: The number takes a singular verb.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: I wish you will pass the test.
r: I hope you pass the test.
y: Hope is for possible things. Wish is for unreal.
a: But: I wish you good luck is fine!
e: I hope it doesn't rain.
I wish I could fly.
q: I ___ you have a great trip!
s: Send this to someone you wish well.

w: The law time is over, so no case.
r: The statute of limitations has run out.
y: It's the legal time limit to start a case.
a: Some crimes have no time limit at all!
e: The statute of limitations is five years.
The case was too old: the statute of limitations had passed.
q: After seven years, the statute of ___ ran out.
The fixed term is statute of limitations.
s: Save this for your legal English.

w: jus-TI-fi-ca-tion
r: jus-ti-fi-CA-tion
y: Stress the part before -tion: CA.
a: The verb moves it: JUS-ti-fy!
e: There's no justification for this.
What is the justification for the cost?
q: Where is the stress in justification?
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: This app is compatible to my phone.
r: This app is compatible with my phone.
y: Compatible with means works together with.
a: People can be compatible too, as partners!
e: Is it compatible with Windows?
They're very compatible with each other.
q: The charger is compatible ___ most phones.
s: Save this for your next tech purchase.

w: We were made wait for hours.
r: We were made to wait for hours.
y: Make someone wait, but be made to wait.
a: The to comes back only in the passive!
e: They made us wait.
He was made to apologize.
m: made us WAIT, were made TO wait
q: She was made ___ the form again.
In the passive, use made to.
s: Save this for your next exam.

w: We follow with the rules.
r: We work in compliance with the rules.
y: In compliance with means obeying a rule or law.
a: Companies have whole teams for compliance!
e: All products are in compliance with safety laws.
Please act in compliance with company policy.
q: The factory is in compliance ___ the law.
The phrase is in compliance with.
s: Save this for your next report.

w: I got a fine. I'm so happy!
r: I got a fine. I have to pay.
y: A fine is money you pay as punishment.
a: I'm fine and a parking fine are very different!
e: She paid a fine for parking there.
The fine was fifty dollars.
q: He got a ___ for driving too fast.
Money as punishment is a fine.
s: Send this to a fast driver.

w: He was accused for lying.
r: He was accused of lying.
y: Accuse someone of something.
a: Blame is different: blame someone for!
e: She accused him of stealing.
They were accused of cheating.
q: He was accused ___ breaking the rules.
s: Save this for your next news story.

w: The dog wagged it's tail.
r: The dog wagged its tail.
y: It's means it is. Its means belonging to it.
a: Try saying it is. If it fails, use its!
e: It's cold today.
The company changed its name.
s: Send this to a friend who writes it's.

w: Cars make green gas.
r: Cars make greenhouse gases.
y: Greenhouse gases trap heat around the Earth.
a: They work like the glass of a greenhouse!
e: Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas.
We must cut greenhouse gas emissions.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: The car collided to a bus.
r: The car collided with a bus.
y: Collide with means crash into.
a: Crash into works too: the car crashed into a bus!
e: Two bikes collided with each other.
The ship collided with a rock.
s: Save this for your next news story.

w: He denied to take the money.
r: He denied taking the money.
y: Deny plus -ing means say you didn't do it.
a: Admit works the same way: admit taking!
e: She denied breaking the glass.
He denies being late.
s: Save this for your next exam.

w: Can we make the meeting later?
r: Can we push back the meeting?
y: Push back means move to a later time.
a: Push back can also mean disagree with a plan!
e: They pushed the launch back a week.
Let's push back lunch to one.
q: The flight was pushed ___ two hours.
s: Save this for your next meeting.

w: The minibar is free, right?
r: Drinks from the minibar cost extra.
y: A minibar is a small hotel fridge. You pay.
a: Some hotels charge if you just move items!
e: I took water from the minibar.
The minibar has snacks and drinks.
q: The small fridge in a hotel room is a ___.
s: Save this before your next hotel stay.

w: Translate this to English.
r: Translate this into English.
y: The standard form is translate into.
a: From A into B: translate from French into English!
e: The book was translated into ten languages.
Can you translate this into Spanish?
q: The standard form is translate into.
s: Send this to a translator friend.

w: Sit besides me.
r: Sit beside me.
y: Beside means next to. Besides means also.
a: One extra S changes the meaning!
e: The lamp is beside the bed.
Besides English, I speak French.
s: Save this and test a friend.

w: Tell me your sick past.
r: Can you tell me your medical history?
y: Medical history means your past health problems.
a: Doctors ask about family history too!
e: The doctor asked about my medical history.
Please fill in your medical history.
s: Save this for your next doctor visit.

w: AS-tro-no-my
r: as-TRO-no-my
y: Stress the second part: TRO.
a: But: as-tro-NO-mi-cal moves it again!
e: She studies astronomy.
Astronomy is the study of stars.
q: Where is the stress in astronomy?
s: Send this to a space fan.

w: My bag is identical than yours.
r: My bag is identical to yours.
y: Identical takes to. Never than.
a: Similar to works the same way!
e: Her dress is identical to mine.
The copy is identical to the original.
q: This phone is identical ___ the old one.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: The school forbids to use phones.
r: The school forbids using phones.
y: No person? Use forbid plus -ing.
a: With a person: forbid students to use phones!
e: The law forbids smoking here.
My parents forbid me to stay out late.
s: Save this for your next exam.

w: Sugar helps to make heart problems.
r: Sugar contributes to heart problems.
y: Contribute to means be one of the causes.
a: It also means give, like money to a charity!
e: Stress can contribute to illness.
Everyone contributed to the project.
q: Bad sleep can contribute ___ weight gain.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: I suggest you to go.
r: I suggest you go.
y: There is no suggest someone to.
a: I suggest going is also correct!
e: I suggest you call him.
She suggested taking a taxi.
q: Suggest you is followed by a base verb.
s: Save this and suggest it to a friend.

w: Junk food causes undernourishment.
r: Junk food can cause malnutrition.
y: Malnutrition is any poor diet. Undernourishment is too little food.
a: Even big eaters can have it!
e: Malnutrition is a problem in poor areas.
Undernourishment means not getting enough food.
m: bad food = MALNUTRITION, too little = UNDERNOURISHMENT
q: A diet of only chips can lead to ___.
s: Save this for your next health essay.

w: The hotel paid our learning tour.
r: Travel agents went on a familiarization trip.
y: It's a free trip so agents can learn a place.
a: People call it a fam trip!
e: The hotel invited us on a familiarization trip.
Our familiarization trip lasted three days.
m: agents learn the place = FAM TRIP
q: Agents visit hotels on a familiarization ___.
s: Save this for your travel career.

w: He won the race. He is the victim.
r: He was the victim of a crime.
y: A victim is someone hurt by a crime or event.
a: Victim is for bad things, never wins!
e: The victims got help.
She was a victim of the flood.
q: The police spoke to the ___ of the robbery.
A victim suffers from a crime.
s: Save this and share it.

w: la-TEN-cy
r: LA-ten-cy
y: Stress the first part: LA, like late.
a: Online players talk about it all the time!
e: The latency is too high.
Low latency makes calls clearer.
q: Where is the stress in latency?
s: Send this to a gamer friend.

w: This model is inferior than that one.
r: This model is inferior to that one.
y: Inferior and superior take to, not than.
a: They already mean worse and better!
e: The copy is inferior to the original.
Their service is superior to ours.
q: This hotel is superior ___ the others.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: I had him to fix my car.
r: I had him fix my car.
y: Have someone do something. No to.
a: Get takes to: I got him to fix it!
e: I'll have my assistant call you.
She had her son clean the room.
q: Have someone do, with no to.
s: Save this for your next exam.

w: Your help was not valuable at all. Thanks!
r: Your help was invaluable. Thank you!
y: Invaluable means very, very useful.
a: In- here doesn't mean not!
e: Your advice was invaluable.
Her support was invaluable to the team.
s: Save this for your next thank-you email.

w: He married with a teacher.
r: He married a teacher.
y: The verb marry needs no word after it.
a: But: he is married to a teacher!
e: She married her best friend.
They're married to each other.
s: Send this to a newly married friend.

w: I love classic music like Mozart.
r: I love classical music like Mozart.
y: Classical is old serious music. Classic means famous and great.
a: A classic car is old and loved!
e: Casablanca is a classic movie.
She plays classical piano.
m: Mozart = CLASSICAL, great old film = CLASSIC
s: Send this to a music lover.

w: Food is part of my culture face.
r: Food is part of my cultural identity.
y: Cultural identity is feeling part of a culture.
a: Language is often the biggest part of it!
e: Music shapes our cultural identity.
Moving abroad changed my cultural identity.
m: who I am + my culture = CULTURAL IDENTITY
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: Consumers make the products.
r: Consumers buy and use the products.
y: A consumer is a person who buys and uses things.
a: You are a consumer every time you shop!
e: Consumers want lower prices.
The law protects consumers.
s: Save this for your next essay.

w: back-PACK-er
r: BACK-pack-er
y: Stress stays on BACK, like in backpack.
a: Adding -er doesn't move the stress!
e: The hostel is full of backpackers.
He traveled as a backpacker.
q: Where is the stress in backpacker?
s: Send this to a travel friend.

w: She is skilled on design.
r: She is skilled in design.
y: Skilled in or at a subject.
a: Good at works the same way!
e: He is skilled in cooking.
We need workers skilled in IT.
s: Save this for your next resume.

w: I propose leave early.
r: I propose to leave early.
y: Propose to plus verb means intend to do it.
a: Propose also means ask someone to marry you!
e: We propose to open a new office.
He proposed to her in Paris.
q: The city proposes ___ a new bridge.
Propose to plus verb means intend.
s: Save this for your next report.

w: I have to go off now.
r: I have to head off now.
y: Head off is a casual way to say leave.
a: Head out means the same thing!
e: I'm heading off. See you!
We headed off to the beach.
q: It's late. I need to head ___.
s: Save this and use it today.

w: She is responsible of the budget.
r: She is responsible for the budget.
y: In charge of something? Responsible for.
a: In charge of uses of. Responsible uses for!
e: Who is responsible for this?
He's responsible for sales.
s: Save this for your next interview.

w: Your welcome!
r: You're welcome!
y: You're means you are.
a: Read it as you are. Does it work? Then you're!
e: You're very kind.
Is this your phone?
q: You are going to love this.
s: Send this to a friend who writes your.

w: This pan is made of no-rust iron.
r: This pan is made of stainless steel.
y: Stainless steel is steel that doesn't rust.
a: Stain-less means no marks!
e: The sink is stainless steel.
I bought a stainless steel bottle.
s: Save this for your next shopping trip.

w: Tie the box with a string of rope.
r: Tie the box with string.
y: String is thin rope.
a: A guitar has strings too!
e: I need some string.
She tied a string around the gift.
s: Save this and share it.

w: IM-mi-gra-tion
r: im-mi-GRA-tion
y: Stress the part before -tion: GRA.
a: Every -tion word works this way!
e: We waited at immigration.
Immigration is a big topic.
q: Where is the stress in immigration?
s: Save this for your next trip.
